title: Buddy Petit and his death
summary: Robinson sometimes played with Petit; Petit died suddenly before a job with Milton.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Did you ever work with Buddy Petit?

Yeah, sometime I worked with him, but I never just played in his band. I used to play extra sometimes. Yeah, exactly. And we used to hire him plenty of times. Because with this little band here, or this last band I played, Ernest Milton. But that's where Buddy was playing second con with the Ernest Milton when he died. Oh, yeah. Yeah. Buddy was supposed to go with him, a place down there that he used to call Burwood. He used to go down there and play with him. Well, that job coming up that Saturday, well, he'd take him sick because he didn't stay sick alone just one day. He died in a sudden.
Yeah, he died in a sudden.

Well, if they went to see him that morning, you told him wait a minute, he'll be able to go. Well, he waited there and he, okay, he wasn't getting no better, so they went on down. When they come back, he was dead, he died that Saturday night. And at the time he died, his friend was Louis Armstrong.
Well, I remember they had, he was the, uh, Paul Bearer. Yeah, honorary Paul Bearer or something, yeah, I remember reading about it, Louis wrote about it in his book.

He had a fine little second hornet that boy had, Buddy Pity. He talked about a harmony in the horn, he had it. He kind of gave Louis Armstrong plenty of ideas when Louis was down here. But Louis used to play on the street down here.
Yes, I heard he did. I think it was the Tuxedo Band, I believe.
